name: Hits from the Sky: Comets, Asteroids and Craters
description: The belt of rocks between Mars and Jupiter, comets from the cold edge of the system, and the impacts that scarred planets and reshaped life.

checkpoints.name: Leftovers of creation
checkpoints.note: The asteroid belt and the Kuiper Belt are leftovers of the solar system's formation. A planet-sized body, Theia, is thought to have hit the young Earth and made the Moon, and the Late Heavy Bombardment may have pelted both.

checkpoints.name: Scars on Earth
checkpoints.note: Vredefort and the Sudbury Basin are huge ancient impact structures. About 66 million years ago the Chicxulub impact led to the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction, ending Tyrannosaurus rex and the other dinosaurs that could not fly.

checkpoints.name: Watching comets
checkpoints.note: Meteor Crater in Arizona was formed about 50,000 years ago. Halley's Comet was recorded for centuries, Tycho Brahe showed in 1577 that comets fly far beyond the Moon, and Edmond Halley showed that comets could return on a regular orbit.

checkpoints.name: Impacts seen
checkpoints.note: Biela's comet broke apart, the 1908 Tunguska event flattened Siberian forest, and in 1994 fragments of Shoemaker-Levy 9 struck Jupiter while telescopes and spacecraft watched. Comet Hale-Bopp was a bright sight in 1997.

checkpoints.name: Landing on a comet
checkpoints.note: In 2013 the Chelyabinsk meteor exploded over Russia and injured more than a thousand people with broken glass. The Rosetta spacecraft reached Comet 67P in 2014 and put a lander on its surface, and Jupiter and the Moon, scarred by impacts, show how common such hits have been.
